issues.claim: T-V4-63 (V04 l. 3156), rewritten this round by R6-02's (V4-8) with VV34-r5-02, adds two clauses that leave an arch vault `collapsed` under a fallen span: 'the circuit's case run again with that `vault` span breached with its chamber first (`ruined`, its arch vault `collapsed`) … (§2.7's crossing table, W1·C6)', and the frame growth's 'each new span taking that end span's `state` … a vault laid in a `ruined` or `cleared` one `collapsed` (V04 §3.5.4 (d) (2))'. Its bar, kept from round 4, still reads 'after each commit every arch vault's key names a standing span of use `vault`'. In the set a standing span is one whose `state` is absent (V06 §3.19.1 (3) 'every span standing or ruined'; V06 §3.19.2 (3) 'each standing span … → breach'; V06 §3.2 l. 1038 'a chamber for each standing `vault` span …, a collapse under a `ruined` or `cleared` span'). V04 §3.5.4 (d) (2)–(3) keep a collapsed vault in a ruined or cleared span; only a span gone, set `open` or under a wall removes it. So after the breach commit and after the frame growth's commit the test's own fixtures hold a collapsed vault keyed to a `ruined` span, and the bar fails on a correct build. One builder keeps the bar and suppresses those vaults, against (d) (1)–(2) and the clause's own words; another reads 'standing' as 'existing'. Two builds.
issues.required_change: T-V4-63's bar 'after each commit every arch vault's key names a standing span of use `vault`' → 'after each commit every arch vault's key names a span of the way whose `use` is `vault` and over which no wall stands — standing, or `ruined` or `cleared` with that vault `collapsed` (V04 §3.5.4 (d) (2))'.

issues.claim: §2.7's support step (7) (base l. 2712–2716) runs '(1)–(5) and the span rule … on the extension alone … to the deck's new end on the new ring, against the obstacles standing then'. (3) (l. 2544–2547) says a merged clear span past `maxClearSpanM` 'drops a generated course (`raised_too_long`, which waits as `raised_too_tall` does, V06 §3.19 (5)) and makes a declared one's dry run bend it'. (4) (l. 2552–2554) says the same for a pier past `maxPierM`. Round 6 wrote that the extension 'keeps the deck's course' and 'is no course laid' (C12 l. 2674–2676; (7)'s last sentence; (M2)'s 'excepted: (7)'), and (6) holds the way ('nothing laid later … drops it'). The frame growth lays new ground and water in the band between the old and new margin (S1, §4.11 *The rung at an epoch*). An extension whose course meets there a river wider than `maxClearSpanM` with no support in its water, or a valley deeper than `maxPierM` (aqueduct 35 m, V11 §3.24.2), has no outcome. Read literally, a generated aqueduct is dropped or 'waits'. But the foot batch has already moved its ring-end foot's ground end onto the new ring (§3.2 (9), l. 3778–3788), so a waiting deck leaves the foot's two ends on different rings, against §3.10's stored-references row ('both ends resolve at every stage end'). A declared way has no dry run at an epoch to bend it. Another builder keeps the course and lays the span or pier past its bound, failing T110-2's 'every clear span and pier within its bound'. Two builds, and no bar runs the case: T110-2's frame clause, T-V4-63 and T-V5-14 extend over open ground.
issues.required_change: (7), after 'against the obstacles standing then,' add: '— where the extension's course meets (3)'s clear-span bound or (4)'s pier bound (a water face or a valley the grown ring reveals), the way, being held ((6)), is neither dropped nor left waiting: the extension's course is bent, as item 101 R2 bends a declared course, to the nearest course from that station to the new ring whose piers and clear spans fit, kept across a band (C12), the ring-end foot's two ends re-placed where that course meets the new rings (§2.7 `RaisedFoot`); with none, it is laid on its course with each span or pier past its bound reported (V06 §2.10's `raised` section) —'. END under scope: T110-2's frame clause adds 'and, on a variant whose grown ring holds, across the aqueduct's course, a river wider than `raisedWays.structure.maxClearSpanM` and, on a second run, a valley deeper than its `maxPierM` — the extension bent to the nearest course whose clear spans and piers fit, the aqueduct kept, nothing waiting, both ends of its ring-end foot on the new rings'. END under V06: §2.10's `raised` section adds `extendedPastBound: number /* frame-growth extensions laid past a support-step bound with no fitting course (§2.7's support step (7)) */`. (If the adjudicator rules the other form instead — the bounds do not apply to an extension, which is no course laid — (7) says so in those words, and T110-2's bound bar reads 'on every course laid'.)

issues.claim: R6-02 wrote two arch-vault clauses into E3 tests: T-V6-11 (l. 4134, (V6-20)) 'V04 laying again the arch vault of a `vault` span the old wall stood over', and T-V6-47's bar (l. 4170, (V6-21)) '0 arch vaults in a `vault` span under a wall'. At an epoch both are V04's `ArchVaults.reconcile` over `EpochScope.raised`, run by V06's `under.extend` (V06 §3.2: 'the epoch-side guarantee … that no chamber stands … under a wall and every `vault` span no wall stands over has its chamber'). V06 §8 builds those adapters at E8 ('the `under.*` adapters over V04's functions with the epoch scope (`raised` and `levelled` included: the arch-vault reconcile …)'), and INDEX §4 has 'E8 after V04's U5'; M6-E starts after M4, and M6-U, which lays the arch vaults, after M5. V06 §8's E3 cell runs T-V6-11 and T-V6-47 whole at E3 (only T-V6-11's sky clause deferred), so before E8 T-V6-11's clause cannot run and T-V6-47's bar holds vacuously. R5-05 (c) and INDEX §5 risk 2 require each such clause to name the first exit after its provider. This is R6-09's class: nothing built changes. VCS-r6-03 raises the same for T110-2's base clauses and VV56-r6-05 the fixture's `vault` spans; neither schedules these two.
issues.required_change: V06 §8's E3 tests cell: '(T-V6-11's sky clause at the later of E3 and V05's P6, which builds the landfall)' → '(T-V6-11's sky clause at the later of E3 and V05's P6, which builds the landfall; T-V6-11's and T-V6-47's arch-vault clauses at E8, which builds the epoch's arch-vault reconcile)'; E8's tests cell 'T-V6-33–40, 50, 51, 55, 56, 64, 67–69; T-V6-27's burial-need clause' adds '; T-V6-11's and T-V6-47's arch-vault clauses'.

issues.claim: repair-r6-V02's hand-off (assemble-r6 §2.1: 'for the adjudicator to route') was routed by no adjudication. T-V3-40 (b) (V03 l. 2907) asserts each building of a returned district draws its look 'exactly in the condition's weeks, and at its own level outside them, after the hand-over (`crisisLookYields`)', and that 'a `disaster` preview draws its ruin over a building under a rebuild Works (a preview never hands over)'. Its timing cell runs (b) 'from P4 once item 122's base parts (M3b) and V01's districts (M5) stand', and V03 §8's P4 cell defers only (b)'s village clause. `crisisLookYields` is built by V06's E2 (V06 §8's E2 row: 'the crisis hand-over (item 122 (a), V06 §3.22 …)'); until then V02 reads X36's stand-in, 'nothing repaired, the look standing until its condition no longer stands' (V02 §8.6). R6-09 scheduled V02's twin clause, T-V2-60's hand-over, at the later of M6b and E2, but not V03's. Graded minor (R6-09's class): nothing built changes; the clause runs before its provider.
